subject: Stakeholder roster + systems scope — follow-up & security kickoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightbridgehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder roster + systems scope — follow-up & security kickoff

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Recap
- Primary use case: inline recommendations inside patient portal and an offline analytics scoring pipeline.
- Tech contacts: Ellen (security/architecture) + Tom (product lead).
- Procurement + legal: Sana (procurement) and Michael Chen (VP Finance) are decision-makers on terms and PO.
- Timeline: goal to complete security intake and procurement review by end of Q3 (your org) to start a pilot in Q4.

Open questions I captured
1) Confirm the systems in scope for the security review (are we limited to patient portal + analytics, or is the ETL layer / data lake also in scope?)
2) Data residency / PHI flow — you flagged some data touching EU systems; need to confirm region constraints.
3) Preferred format for the questionnaire — PDF download vs. shared Google form.

Attachments / links
- I’ve attached the Redwood security questionnaire (PDF) for you to review; we can accept a partially completed copy if you want to iterate.
- HubSpot link to the account record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/BBH-2027-019

Proposed next steps (short and actionable)
- Ellen: confirm in-scope systems and whether ETL/data lake are included (reply inline).
- Tom / Michael: confirm procurement timeline and whether PO/standard SOW will be required.
- BrightBridge procurement: can you nominate the procurement contact who will receive the contract & vendor form? (Sana listed?)
- From Redwood: Marissa will draft an architecture MVP diagram and Rishi will prepare initial answers for the questionnaire sections related to encryption, retention, and SOC2 evidence.

If that sounds right, we’ll aim to turn around the first-pass questionnaire responses within 3 business days after you confirm scope.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: brightbridge_security_questionnaire.pdf

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightbridgehealth.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder roster + systems scope — follow-up & security kickoff

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications inline:

On Thu, 10 Jun 2027 at 3:12 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recap
> - Primary use case: inline recommendations inside patient portal and an offline analytics scoring pipeline.

Confirm: patient portal and the analytics scoring service are in scope. The ETL jobs that land data in our internal data lake are out-of-scope for this initial intake — that will be a separate vendor review later this year.

> - Tech contacts: Ellen (security/architecture) + Tom (product lead).
I’ll be the security intake owner for now. Tom is the product owner.

> - Procurement + legal: Sana (procurement) and Michael Chen (VP Finance) are decision-makers on terms and PO.
Correction: Michael Chen is VP, Finance and is the economic approver for new vendor spend >$50k. Sana Patel (cc’d) is the procurement lead — she’ll own vendor paperwork.

> Timeline: goal to complete security intake and procurement review by end of Q3 (your org) to start a pilot in Q4.
That timeline still looks right from our side, assuming we don’t need deep infra changes.

> Open questions I captured
> 1) Confirm the systems in scope for the security review (are we limited to patient portal + analytics, or is the ETL layer / data lake also in scope?)
Answered above — ETL/data lake out of scope.

> 2) Data residency / PHI flow — you flagged some data touching EU systems; need to confirm region constraints.
We store some historical telemetry in our EU analytics cluster. For the initial pilot, no EU PHI should be forwarded to Redwood. We’ll mark the EU dataset as out-of-scope for now — that simplifies the intake.

> 3) Preferred format for the questionnaire — PDF download vs. shared Google form.
Procurement prefers a completed PDF for their vendor file.

Next step for Redwood: please return a filled copy of pages 2–6 (security & controls, encryption, retention, SOC2 evidence) and we’ll loop in procurement for contract terms.

Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Security Architecture — BrightBridge Health
ellen.park@brightbridgehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightbridgehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@brightbridgehealth.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@brightbridgehealth.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stakeholder roster + systems scope — follow-up & security kickoff

Appreciate the clarifications, Ellen — that makes the scope clearer and helps the intake. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) We’ll produce a filled-first-pass of pages 2–6 of the PDF questionnaire (security controls, encryption, retention, SOC2 evidence). Expect that by Tue 15 Jun EOD.
2) Marissa will drop a simple MVP architecture diagram (PNG) that highlights the patient portal and scoring service boundaries; she’ll exclude ETL/data lake.
3) Rishi (cc’d) — can you prioritize the SOC2/evidence and encryption sections? Specific asks: key rotation/KMS approach; network isolation diagrams we can attach; sample SOC2 control IDs we map to the questionnaire.

Sana / Michael — once we turn around the questionnaire, we’d appreciate any vendor-form/PO instructions so we can align our contract team (happy to use your standard MSA + SOW or a one-off PO).

We’ll attach: brightbridge_security_questionnaire.pdf (filled-first-pass), mvp_arch_diagram.png, and RBW_Sec_Notes_BrightBridge.pdf (internal notes).

If you prefer a working Google doc instead of PDF iteration, say the word — otherwise we’ll send the PDF per procurement preference.

Thanks —
Ben

Attachments: brightbridge_security_questionnaire.pdf, mvp_arch_diagram.png, RBW_Sec_Notes_BrightBridge.pdf

- Rishi: complete the encryption, key management, retention, and SOC2 evidence sections in the attached questionnaire (see pages 2–6). Flag any gaps we can’t answer without a short technical kickoff.
- Marissa: put together a one-slide architecture diagram (mvp_arch_diagram.png) that clearly labels in-scope components and data flows (exclude ETL/data lake). Procurement wants clear boundaries.

I’ve attached our internal notes (RBW_Sec_Notes_BrightBridge.pdf) with suggested answers; please review and update.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — I’ll coordinate with Ellen once we have the filled first pass.

—Ben

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Stakeholder roster + systems scope — follow-up & security kickoff

On Mon, 14 Jun 2027 at 08:01 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rishi / Marissa — forwarding the thread. High priority asks before Tue EOD:

Thanks — I reviewed the questionnaire and updated our internal notes. Quick notes for Ben / Ellen: 
- Encryption: Redwood uses customer-specific KMS keys (KMS-backed envelope encryption). We rotate data keys every 90 days by default; customer-managed CMKs are supported.
- Network: inference clusters run in isolated VPCs with restricted egress; control plane communicates over mTLS.
- SOC2: we reference our latest SOC2 Type II report (report id: RBW-SOC2-2026, available upon NDA).
- Retention: default logs retained 90 days; customer-configurable token and KV cache retention via the Console (we document expected retention windows in the questionnaire).

I attached RBW_Sec_Notes_BrightBridge.pdf with suggested language for pages 2–6. I’ll sync with Marissa on the diagram details.

Deliverables: RBW_Sec_Notes_BrightBridge.pdf attached. I can deliver the completed questionnaire PDF tomorrow AM if we’re aligned.

—Rishi
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
